(Tacoma, Washington) | college = * [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] (2016–2018) * [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2020 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2020]]) * [[Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Mountain West Player of the Year]] (2020) * First-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] (2020) * Mountain West Defensive Player of the Year (2020) }} '''Malachi Flynn''' (born May 10, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] and the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]]. ==High school career== Flynn is the youngest of seven children. He stood 5'2 in his freshman season in high school, then grew to 5'6 as a sophomore before a growth spurt made him his current height of 6'1.{{cite news |last1=Bennett |first1=Brian |title=Malachi Flynn is the transfer who is leading surprising San Diego State |url=https://theathletic.com/1475593/2019/12/20/malachi-flynn-is-the-transfer-that-is-leading-surprising-san-diego-state/ |accessdate=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=December 20, 2019}} As a senior at [[Bellarmine Preparatory School|Bellarmine Prep]], Flynn averaged 29.7 points, 6.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game, while shooting 48 percent from the floor. He earned a host of accolades, including [[The News Tribune]]'s All-Area player of the year, [[Associated Press]] Washington player of the year, the Class 4A player of the year by the Washington Interscholastic Basketball Coaches Association, and the 4A Narrows League MVP as a senior. His 743 points as a senior set the single-season mark at Bellarmine Prep, and he finished with 1,625 career points, second to [[Abdul Gaddy]].{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Lauren |title=Former Bellarmine Prep, WSU standout announces transfer to San Diego State |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article210642879.html |accessdate=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The News Tribune]] |date=May 7, 2018}} Flynn originally committed to [[Pacific Tigers men's basketball|Pacific]] before reopening his recruitment late in the signing period.{{cite news |last1=Milles |first1=Todd |title=WSU’s late find — Flynn — a basketball life saver |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/college/washington-state-university/article124018714.html |accessdate=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The News Tribune]] |date=December 31, 2016}} He signed with the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] on April 13, 2016.{{cite news |last1=Thorpe |first1=Jacob |title=Kent effusive about newest recruit Malachi Flynn |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2016/apr/13/kent-effusive-about-newest-recruit-malachi-flynn/ |accessdate=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=April 3, 2016}} ==College career== In November 2016, Flynn scored 27 points in an 83–76 victory over [[Utah Valley Wolverines men's basketball|Utah Valley]], which is sixth most for a Cougar freshman in history. As a freshman at Washington State, he averaged 9.7 points per game and shot 38.7 percent from three-point range. Flynn averaged 15.8 points and 4.3 assists per game while shooting 41.3 percent from the field as a sophomore. He was the top player on a team that finished 12–19. Following the season, Flynn announced he was transferring. After receiving interest from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] and [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], Flynn signed with [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] in May 2018.{{cite news |last1=Zarrett |first1=E. Jay |title=Former Washington State guard Malachi Flynn transferring to San Diego State |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/former-washington-state-guard-malachi-flynn-transferring-san-diego-state-creighton-baylor-texas-am/6olkxpdhb3cb18t8j2ka0abhw |accessdate=January 2, 2020 |work=[[Sporting News]] |date=May 7, 2018}} Coming into his redshirt junior season, Flynn was named the preseason [[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] player of the year by Mountain West Wire.{{cite news |last1=Maciejewski |first1=Michael |title=The Case For Malachi Flynn As Mountain West's Best Player |url=https://mwwire.com/2019/10/16/the-case-for-malachi-flynn-as-mountain-wests-best-player/ |accessdate=January 2, 2020 |work=Mountain West Wire |date=October 16, 2019}} In a game in which he otherwise shot poorly, Flynn hit a last-second three-point shot on December 8 to defeat [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]] 59–57.{{cite news |last1=Zeigler |first1=Mark |title=Aztecs survive against San Jose State on late 3 by Malachi Flynn |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2019-12-08/aztecs-survive-against-san-jose-state-on-late-3-by-malachi-flynn |accessdate=January 2, 2020 |work=[[San Diego Union Tribune]] |date=December 8, 2019}} He was named to the midseason watchlist for the [[Wooden Award]].{{cite news |title=Gonzaga's Filip Petrusev among new faces on Wooden Award midseason list |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28448986/gonzaga-filip-petrusev-new-faces-wooden-award-midseason-list |accessdate=January 10, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=January 8, 2020}} On February 29, 2020, Flynn scored a career-high 36 points, the most by any Aztec since 2005, shooting 13-of-20 from the floor in a 83–76 comeback win over [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]].{{cite news |title=No. 5 San Diego St. overcomes 2nd-half deficit, tops Nevada |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401173804 |accessdate=March 1, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 29, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Flynn was named [[Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Mountain West Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2020/3/3/mountain-west-announces-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx |title=Mountain West Announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=March 3, 2020 |accessdate=March 3, 2020}} He averaged 17.6 points, 5.1 assists, and 4.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=NBC Sports College Basketball All-American Teams |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/03/10/college-basketball-all-american-teams/ |accessdate=March 16, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 10, 2020}} Following the season, Flynn declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=San Diego State's Malachi Flynn entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29049281/san-diego-state-malachi-flynn-entering-nba-draft |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 17, 2020}} ==Career
